title: BLE Connection Lifecycle
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Robotics and Computational Thinking
description: A p5.js step-through of a Bluetooth Low Energy connection between a leader (central) and a follower (peripheral) robot. Two state machines highlight the current state in gold, a middle column shows the radio packet on the air, event badges show IRQ codes, a code strip shows the MicroPython call for each step, and a log shows what each robot prints. Students can send commands, walk out of range, or change the advertising name.

educational.topic: BLE connection lifecycle and IRQ event handling
learningObjectives: Put the BLE connection steps in order: advertise, scan, connect, write, disconnect
Match each step to the IRQ event code that fires on the leader or the follower
Match each step to the MicroPython call in the leader and follower code
Explain why a wrong advertising name or walking out of range stops the connection
prerequisites: Central and peripheral roles, IRQ callbacks, and the leader and follower code from Chapter 12
if/elif branches and functions from Chapter 4

controls.purpose: Start over with the follower advertising and the leader idle

controls.purpose: Write b"FORWARD" when both robots are connected

controls.label: Send STOP

controls.purpose: Show a plain-language definition of a state

simulation.modelType: Two coupled finite-state machines driven by BLE events
variables: last IRQ event on each robot
assumptions: Event codes match the constants in the Chapter 12 code: 1, 2, 3 on the follower and 5, 7, 8, 17 on the leader
The leader connects only if the advertising data contains b"RobotFollower"
The leader code does not restart scanning after a disconnect, as in the chapter
limitations: Service discovery (finding value_handle) is not shown
Timing values in the log are illustrative

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Worked example with step-through and failure cases
pedagogical.interactionPattern: Next Step / Auto Play state machines with clickable states and event buttons
keyQuestions: Why do the leader and follower get different event codes for the same connection?
Which event makes the follower start advertising again?
Why does the leader never connect to Robot2?
Where would you add code so the leader reconnects after a disconnect?
commonMisconceptions: Both robots get the same event code when they connect
The leader automatically scans again after a disconnect
The follower reads commands by polling instead of through the _IRQ_GATTS_WRITE event
assessmentOpportunities: Annotated leader and follower code with step numbers
Event code table for both robots
Exit ticket ordering four events with their codes
